articles.title: Repeat offender landlords fined over £200,000 in total
articles.summary: Two landlords have been fined over £216,000 after renting out homes in a dangerous condition.  The penalties relate to properties in Norfolk following a crackdown by Breckland council officers on homes owned by repeat-offending landlords. One landlord, who lets 11 properties in the area, was fined £64,800 for failing to carry out electrical safety checks. […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Two landlords in Norfolk face fines exceeding £216,000 for renting unsafe properties, following a crackdown by Breckland council on repeat offenders.  
- One landlord, managing 11 homes, received a hefty £64,800 penalty for neglecting mandatory electrical safety checks.

articles.title: Upward-only rent review ban could create a two-tier market – claim
articles.summary: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 received Royal Assent in April
articles.ai_summary:
- The recent Royal Assent of the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 introduces a ban on upward-only rent reviews, igniting concerns over potential market disparities.  
- Analysts warn this legislation could lead to a two-tier rental market, impacting landlords and tenants differently across the UK.
